justification: The ghost faithfully reconstructs the original's core claims through paraphrase: (1) the boundary-definition seam in the golden rule ('whoever defines the whole defines the good' → 'the one who gets to draw the line around what counts as the whole thereby decides what counts as good'); (2) the co-equal second law forbidding unilateral self-boundary-judgment ('no node adjudicates the boundary of the whole alone' → 'no single part may settle, on its own, where the boundary of the whole lies'); (3) the rationale that external judgment prevents the first from becoming a license ('keeps the first from becoming a license' → 'could be turned into a permission slip'); (4) the external/transcendent source of boundary authority ('always checked from outside' → 'That call always comes from beyond the part making it'). The ghost also adds interpretive texture ('sits in judgement of its own scope' as a gloss on the mechanism) and restructures for rhetorical clarity, but introduces no new semantic content and drops no substantive claim. The final claim about the status of this second law—'ratified, not provisional' vs 'settled, not still open'—conveys the same assertion of finality and non-negotiability through synonymous language. No material loss, no material addition.
